summary: The prepared base already contains the issue-specific fix from merged upstream PR #38830: expert_pack_mxfp4 now uses SGLang load_jit instead of torch.utils.cpp_extension.load, replacing legacy FileBaton existence-based ownership with kernel-released fcntl.flock. Added deterministic regression coverage for an orphaned lock file and a lock-holder process that dies. The original H200 intermittent CI event could not be exercised on the assigned AMD gfx950 GPU.

tests.what_was_measured: 44 CPU-only JIT cache tests passed, including live-owner exclusion, orphan-file tolerance, and release after holder-process termination.
The prepared PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 FileBaton remained blocked on a pre-existing ownerless lock file until the external timeout, reproducing the reported lock failure mechanism deterministically.

The actual cold MXFP4 JIT path targeted gfx950 but all four tests stopped at compilation because the NVIDIA-specific source includes cuda_bf16.h, which is unavailable in the prepared ROCm toolchain; no MXFP4 GPU kernel executed.

gpu_execution_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) was visible and the test reached hipcc with --offload-arch=gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, but compilation failed at cuda_bf16.h before any MXFP4 kernel or numerical comparison ran. See reports/j-8304b6dcd6ee/raw/mxfp4_gfx950_cold.txt.
remaining_limitations: No H200/NVIDIA GPU was available, so the original intermittent H200 CI hang was not reproduced statistically or end-to-end on its reported architecture.
The assigned gfx950 ROCm environment cannot compile this NVIDIA-specific MXFP4 source because cuda_bf16.h is unavailable; therefore GPU numerical correctness was not claimed.

The evidence verifies the reported stale-file mechanism and the current advisory-lock recovery property, but cannot exclude unrelated compiler or kernel stalls as alternate causes of historical 30-minute jobs.
